source_review.verdict: No source-level blocker found for the scoped terminal receipt claim fix.
invariants: One mutex protects readiness and the consumed bit; a premature claim does not set consumed.
An acquired Arc remains claimable at most once after eviction of its discovery-index entry.
The production wait consumer returns the child result only after a successful claim, including the child-error path; the losing consumer receives the already-consumed error.
Pointer-equal index removal cannot delete a replacement entry with the same textual spawn_id.
Dropping a pending wait future never calls consume; the existing detached monitor still owns the JoinHandle.
Notify registration is enabled before reading result; no new lost-wakeup window is introduced.
Registry-to-outcome mutex order is consistent with reserve; complete and outcome wait do not acquire the registry mutex.
After outcome.wait resolves, no additional await occurs before registry claim and the production wait return; this does not imply durable/exactly-once downstream delivery.
Active caps, oldest-ready eviction and non-evictable control-plane entries are unchanged.
Receipt ownership is not descendant effect quiescence or worktree cleanup authority.
source_review.regression_limits: Deterministic source scenarios, not an executed scheduler/concurrency stress proof.

remaining_gates: Applicable real process_agent_pool/process_agent_control boundaries using the existing runner and current fixtures
limits: Selected source slice, not full checkout compilation
At-most-once receipt claim, not a durable or unlimited result store
